open_points.subject: FlowVersion identity
open_points.text: “order-free lists sorted before hashing — … edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)”
open_points.question: How are edges or constants ordered for identity when the stated keys tie, especially valid parallel edges with the same endpoints but different guards and multiple constants targeting the same port?
options: Add canonical JSON of the complete edge or constant as a tie-breaker
Preserve submission order among ties
Refuse tied edge or constant keys before computing identity
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical JSON of the complete item as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case
open_points.text: “input values by port, optional expected outputs” and “Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size”
open_points.question: Must authored inputs contain exactly every input port and no unknown ports, and, when expected outputs are present, must they contain exactly every output port or may they specify only a subset?
options: Require exact complete mappings for inputs and expected outputs
Require all inputs but allow partial expected outputs
Ignore unknown entries and compare only supplied expected outputs
open_points.default_guess: Require exact complete mappings, with expected_outputs either wholly absent or complete.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case file fixtures
open_points.text: “input values by port, optional expected outputs” versus `fit_port_value`, which receives file facts “digest, size and media type — never bytes”, while `trial_case_added` must persist fixture bytes
open_points.question: For an authored file fixture, what does the operation receive, who computes its digest and size, and are caller-supplied file facts trusted, checked against supplied bytes, or generated by the kernel?
options: Receive bytes plus media type and have the kernel compute digest and size
Receive bytes with claimed digest and size and verify them
Receive a pre-existing uploaded-file reference
open_points.default_guess: Receive bytes and media type, with the kernel computing digest and size before validation and storage.

open_points.subject: Manifest source
open_points.question: How does a binding operation obtain a file at `manifest_revision`: is the location a checked-out immutable directory, a Git repository queried by revision, or a revision-addressed directory layout, and what failures does that access produce?
options: Require `manifest_location` to expose the configured revision as an immutable directory
Read the file from a Git object at the configured revision
Resolve the revision through a specified revision-to-directory layout
open_points.default_guess: Treat the configured location as an immutable snapshot and verify that it identifies the configured revision.

open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request base URL
open_points.text: “The URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path” while proposal validation requires only “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”
open_points.question: Which base-URL forms are valid, and exactly how are paths joined when the base URL has a path, multiple trailing slashes, user information, a query, or a fragment?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port, with no path, query, fragment or user information
Allow a path prefix and define exact slash removal and joining
Delegate joining and normalization to the HTTP library
open_points.default_guess: Allow only scheme, host and optional port, then append the declared absolute path.

open_points.subject: Multipart request construction
open_points.text: “`Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with `filename="<port>"` added for a file part” and “`Content-Type`, the port's media type … without parameters”
open_points.question: What syntax is allowed for port names and file media types used in multipart headers, and must invalid or escapable quotes, control characters, parameters and other header-sensitive characters be refused or encoded?
options: Restrict port names and media types to closed safe syntaxes
Define RFC-compliant quoting and escaping
Refuse multipart use when either value needs escaping
open_points.default_guess: Require a safe token-like port-name syntax and a valid parameter-free type/subtype media type.

open_points.subject: get_repair_view pagination
open_points.text: “a continuation token that also carries the implementation set of its first page” together with “every other string anywhere in the request, at most `bounded_text_bytes_max`” and an unbounded implementation history
open_points.question: How can the continuation token represent an arbitrarily large frozen implementation set while remaining within the request string bound, and what happens when the set cannot fit?
options: Encode a fixed-size snapshot identifier backed by durable server state
Encode a cutoff position from which the implementation set can be reconstructed
Raise the bound or refuse pagination when the token would exceed it
Embed the whole set and accept that some valid histories cannot be paged
open_points.default_guess: Encode the slot plus a store-position cutoff and reconstruct the frozen implementation set from records at or below that cutoff.
